LESSON MENU
Induction is the generation of AC current by changing a magnetic field (flux variation)..
DISCUSSION
If the flux variation is low, induction is low and only a small amount of current is produced.
If the flux variation is high, induction is high and a larger amount of current is produced.
You learned in DC that magnets produce a magnetic field....
When two unlike poles are brought together a pulling force is generated.
When two like poles are brought together a pushing force is generated.
The force produced by a magnetic field is measured in the density of flux lines developed.
More flux lines create a stronger magnetic field and allow for higher induction.
Fewer flux lines create a weaker magnetic field and allow for lower induction.
In order to induce current, three things are required:
Current is induced by moving a conductor through a stationary magnetic field. - a conductor
Current can also be induced by moving a magnetic field around a stationary conductor. - a conductor
Wire is a common conductor. Placing a wire into a magnetic field produces a small electrical current.
Moving the wire through the magnetic field disturbs the flux lines and creates a larger current.
The magnetic field produced expands outward from the center of the conductor.

GENERATING AC POWER
AC power is generated by moving a conductor through a magnetic field.
DISCUSSION
When the conductor and magnetic field are stationary, no voltage is developed.
Moving either the conductor or the magnetic field will produce voltage in the conductor.
In this example the conductor is moved through a stationary magnetic field.
circle graph and the sine wave line graph are provided to help you visualize the operation.
Rotating the conductor 1/4 turn cuts the maximum number of flux lines. The induced voltage is 10 volts.
The circle graph indicates the conductor is at the 90
position. The line graph shows a positive 1/4 cycle sine wave.
As the conductor rotates 1/2 turn, fewer flux lines are cut. The induced voltage reduces to 0 volts.
The graph shows that voltage is zero at 0
Continuing the rotation 3/4 turns induces 10 volts again. Notice however, the polarity is negative.
The graph shows that voltage is maximum at 90
Completing 1 full rotation or one cycle reduces the voltage to 0 volts again.
Note that one complete rotation developed one complete sine wave.
If one rotation occurs each second, what is the frequency of this sine wave?
Remember, the frequency of a sine wave is determined by the number of cycles that occur in 1 second. If only 1 cycle occurs, then the frequency is 1 Hz.
TRY AGAIN!
FREQUENCY - Frequency is determined by the number of cycles that occur in one second. In this example 3 cycles occur in 1 second producing a frequency of 3 Hz.
As the generator rotates faster more cycles per second are developed. The frequency increases as cycles increase.
Slowing the generator's rotation decreases the cycles per second and lowers the frequency.
